chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn Sulayman said:

I wrote to him: May I be your ransom, a man had a slave boy and a slave girl. He married his slave boy to his slave girl, then the master had intercourse with her. Is anything required in that matter? He said: It is not appropriate for him to touch her until the boy divorces her. And this does not contradict the first report, which is that if both were his slaves, the separation is up to him, because he was prevented from having intercourse with her only as long as she was in the bonds of the slave before they were separated, because that is not permissible. And it is permissible for him only if he separates between them and she observes the waiting period of the divorced slave woman from him. Then at that time he may have intercourse with her. And his saying 'until the boy divorces her' means that she becomes clear from him and enters the ruling of the divorced woman for whom divorce is valid, and that is by the separation which we mentioned, and that which indicates that his divorce is effective if he is married to a slave woman other than his master's or to a free woman.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master having intercourse with his slave girl who is married to his slave boy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the nuanced fiqh of 'tamlik al-tasrif' (granting authority) in slave marriages, establishing that while the master retains ultimate control over the female slave, he must wait for the slave's divorce to be legally finalized before exercising his right of intercourse. It distinguishes between the physical possession of the slave and the legal status of the marriage bond, emphasizing that the master's right to consummate the union is contingent upon the completion of the 'iddah' (waiting period) following the slave's divorce. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the master's authority is not immediate but requires the procedural completion of the divorce act by the slave.
